Reference Number: POC-6E16FAD700-45453
Date of Notice: 2026-08-04
Requested Service: Bunion surgery (hallux valgus correction), CPT 28296
Treating Surgeon: [Dr.] Duval, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Aetna Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 28296 (correction of hallux valgus with bunionectomy and proximal metatarsal osteotomy), communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-04. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity."

Aetna's own published medical policy governing this procedure is Clinical Policy Bulletin Number 0629, "Bunionectomy" (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0629.html). I have reviewed the "Bony Correction Bunionectomy" section of that bulletin, which applies to procedures including "proximal metatarsal osteotomy procedures" such as CPT 28296. I am submitting this appeal, together with the enclosed clinical records, to address each element of that criteria set directly. I note that I was not able to confirm the specific "Last Review"/"Effective" date currently in force for CPB 0629 from the copy of the policy I obtained; Aetna is asked to confirm the version and effective date of the policy actually applied to this request [effective/last-revised date of CPB 0629 applied to this determination – not contained in records provided].

Below is a point-by-point mapping of the enclosed clinical documentation to the policy's stated criteria. All text in quotation marks below is quoted directly from CPB 0629 as I retrieved it; nothing has been paraphrased or invented.

1. Six-month conservative treatment trial
The policy states that bony correction bunionectomy is medically necessary when "[t]he member's pain and symptoms over the medial bony eminence or calluses persist, making walking difficult despite at least a 6-month trial of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional that includes the following: Protective cushions/pads; Shoe inserts (generally contractually excluded); Corticosteroid injections; Debridement of hyperkeratotic lesions; Oral analgesics or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs); Alternative or modified footwear that must include the following: Wearing well-fitting, low-heeled comfortable shoes made out of soft materials (e.g., canvas, cloth, soft leather) with wide toe box and padding; or Lace-ups or a combination last (front of the shoe is wider than the back of the shoe) that conforms to the bunion and minimizes irritation."

The record supports this element as follows:
- Symptom duration: 24 months of progressive foot pain, unrelieved by rest — well in excess of the 6-month minimum.
- NSAIDs: 6 months of use with inadequate relief, satisfying the "Oral analgesics or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)" element.
- Corticosteroid injection: administered 2026-03-25, giving 4 weeks of partial relief, satisfying the "Corticosteroid injections" element.
- Alternative/modified footwear: wide toe-box footwear, satisfying the "Alternative or modified footwear ... with wide toe box and padding" element.
- Shoe inserts: a custom orthotic was used for 10 weeks (2026-04-12 to 2026-06-21, 18 visits, per the physical therapy discharge note), satisfying the "Shoe inserts" element.
- Activity modification was also documented during this period.

I recognize that the discrete physical-therapy/orthotic program (10 weeks) is shorter than 6 months standing alone; however, it was undertaken in combination with 6 months of NSAID therapy and a corticosteroid injection, over a total symptom period of 24 months, all under the direction of treating clinicians. Taken together, the enclosed records document a conservative treatment course under professional direction that spans well beyond 6 months and includes each of the modalities the policy lists. If Aetna's reviewers require the orthotic/footwear/activity-modification component itself to span a continuous 6-month period, please identify that requirement specifically so it can be addressed, since I could not locate that specific durational requirement stated for each individual modality in the policy text I retrieved.

2. Radiographic criteria
The policy states: "Radiographic confirmation ... of the most recent weight-bearing view X-ray demonstrating both of the following: An HVA of 30 degrees or greater; and An inter-metatarsal angle (IMA) (formed by the long axis of the first and second metatarsals) of 12 degrees or greater." It further specifies: "Radiographic confirmation must include interpretation and report of weight bearing anterior/posterior and lateral views of the affected foot."

The enclosed weight-bearing foot radiographs dated 2026-06-29 document a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees, both exceeding the policy's stated thresholds (≥30 degrees and ≥12 degrees, respectively). Please confirm that the imaging report of record includes the required anterior/posterior and lateral weight-bearing views; if any additional view or interpretation is needed, we ask that Aetna specify exactly what is missing so it can be supplied. [Confirmation that the 2026-06-29 radiology report explicitly states "weight-bearing anterior/posterior and lateral views" – not contained in the clinical summary provided]

3. Skeletal maturity
The policy requires "[d]ocumentation of skeletal maturity" for bony correction bunionectomy. The clinical summary provided to me for this appeal does not contain an explicit statement of the patient's age or skeletal maturity. [Statement or chart documentation confirming skeletal maturity/closed epiphyses, or date of birth confirming age 18 or older – not contained in records provided]. We ask that the treating surgeon's office supplement the file with this specific documentation if it is not already present, and request that Aetna identify whether this was, in fact, the missing element that led to the "incomplete documentation" determination.

4. Additional qualifying finding
The policy requires that, in addition to the above, "[t]he member has one or more of the following: A neuroma secondary to the bunion; or Problems with a dorsiflexed second toe due to over-riding of the great toe (so-called cross-over toe deformity); or Limited or painful range of motion at the first toe MTP joint; or Painful prominence of the dorsiflexed second toe due to pressure from the first toe; or Ulceration caused by bunion; or Recurrent bursitis; or Demonstration of osteoarthritis on X-ray ...; or The need for relief of a predisposing factor."

The enclosed examination note documents "positive provocative testing on the affected side" and "range of motion limited by pain," which corresponds to the policy's listed finding of "Limited or painful range of motion at the first toe MTP joint." I am also providing the clinical note describing ulceration risk over the bony prominence; I want to be precise that the record as summarized to me describes a risk of ulceration rather than a documented, existing ulceration, so I am not asserting that this alone satisfies the "Ulceration caused by bunion" listed finding — only that the limited/painful range of motion finding is directly documented and matches the policy's list.

5. Exclusionary conditions do not apply
The policy states that bony correction bunionectomy is "not medically necessary for the following indications: Foot ulcer(s) secondary to peripheral vascular disease; or Gangrene of the foot, ankle or lower leg; or Non-ambulatory individuals unless being performed to relieve ulceration due to prominence; or Open blisters, pressure sores, and skin ulceration overlying the bunion when the bunion is not the cause of the skin lesion ...; or Poor tissues at the operative site due to excessive scarring and multiple closely placed previous incisions; or Severe vascular insufficiency significantly impairing circulation to the foot (e.g., absent foot pulses, intermittent claudication, ankle/arm ratio less than 0.6); or To improve the appearance of the foot (cosmetic)."

None of these exclusions apply to this patient: there is no active infection, no gangrene, no documented severe vascular insufficiency, and the patient is ambulatory. The surgery is being requested to address documented pain, functional limitation, and ulceration risk — not for cosmetic reasons.

Enclosed Records
- Physical therapy discharge note documenting the 10-week orthotic/activity-modification program (2026-04-12 to 2026-06-21, 18 visits)
- Medication record documenting 6 months of NSAID use
- Procedure note documenting corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-25 and its outcome
- Weight-bearing foot radiograph report dated 2026-06-29 (HVA 38°, IMA 17°)
- Clinic examination note documenting provocative testing, pain-limited range of motion, and ulceration risk
- [Documentation of skeletal maturity/age, if separately available – not contained in records provided]
- Surgeon's letter of medical necessity from Dr. Duval [to be enclosed if not already submitted]

Request

Because the enclosed records address each documented criterion in Aetna's own Bunionectomy policy (CPB 0629) that I was able to retrieve and quote above, I ask that Aetna reverse the denial and approve CPT 28296 as requested. If any specific element remains missing in Aetna's view, I ask that Aetna identify that element precisely, in writing, so that it can be supplied before the appeal deadline.

I understand that this appeal must be received by 2027-01-31, consistent with the 180-day appeal window stated in the notice of denial. Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise of any additional steps needed.

I have not received a copy of the exact address, fax number, or online portal for submitting this appeal beyond what may appear on the original notice; I am relying on the address printed on that notice and/or the phone number on my Aetna member ID card to direct this submission. Please advise if this appeal should instead be routed elsewhere. [Specific appeal submission address/fax/portal – not contained in records provided]

I also request that Aetna provide, in writing, the complete text and citation (including effective date) of the specific internal medical policy or clinical review criteria actually used to review this request, to the extent it differs from the publicly posted CPB 0629 referenced above.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Quinn Jennings
